title: The 10 Best Wet Tile Saws
subtitle: 7-inch tabletop, 10-inch sliding and handheld wet saws for ceramic, porcelain and stone, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A wet tile saw cuts ceramic, porcelain and stone cleanly with a water-cooled diamond blade that keeps dust down and the blade from overheating. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a sliding cutting cart, capacity for 18-inch tile or larger, water containment and a stand). 7-inch tabletop saws handle backsplashes and bathroom floors; 10-inch sliding saws cut large-format porcelain and planks dead straight. They run from about $101 for VEVOR's 7-inch to $1,379 for DEWALT's D36000S.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: Hoteche 8-Inch Wet Tile Saw, 8A Benchtop Masonry Cutting Tool with Stand
avoid.flag: Rated 1.9; listing recommends it for wood
avoid.verdict: A $310 tile saw rated 1.9 stars whose listing can't decide what it cuts. The PORTER-CABLE PCE980 costs $51 less with a sliding cart and 4.4 stars.
reasons: It's rated 1.9 stars, far below every tile saw we compared.
The spec table lists its recommended surface as 'Wood' and its blade as high speed steel, for a wet saw meant for tile and stone.
It describes a 'saw body tilting range of 45-90°' while competing saws bevel 0-45°, so the listing's details don't hold together.

buyers_guide.a: 7-inch tabletop saws cut 12-inch tile and smaller and suit backsplashes and bathrooms. 10-inch sliding saws carry the tile on a cart past the blade, which gives straighter cuts on large-format porcelain and planks.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a handheld wet saw?
buyers_guide.a: Handheld wet saws cut tile that's already installed, notches, countertops and stone. Most tilers use one alongside a tabletop or sliding saw.
Use a continuous-rim diamond blade for clean porcelain and ceramic cuts. Porcelain is hard and brittle, so a porcelain-specific blade chips less.
Feed slowly, keep the water flowing, support the whole tile and cut with the glazed face up. A fresh, sharp blade helps most.

buyers_guide.q: Can I use a wet saw indoors?
buyers_guide.a: Yes, with a splash guard or containment like SKIL's HydroLock and a drop cloth. Wet cutting keeps silica dust down, which matters for your lungs.
